findings.title: Reduced-motion assertion cannot detect a broken production freeze offset
findings.description: Check 6 validates the local literal 22 against BEAT instead of exercising startDashboard. Changing only the production freeze offset from 22 seconds to zero removes the posted user text from the reduced-motion frame, while every assertion in assert-sim still passes and prints the same output. This is a confirmed coverage hole, not evidence that the frozen baseline currently renders the wrong frame.
findings.evidence: website-review-probe.json: both suite exits are zero; baseline generated HTML has the posted user message, the freeze-at-zero mutation does not. The browser brand tests do not exercise reduced-motion rendering.
findings.recommendation: Exercise startDashboard with reduced-motion enabled and assert the posted user message and agent reply in its rendered output. Exporting a shared offset can remove the duplicate literal but does not alone verify rendering.
findings.refactor_hint: Keep the marketing simulation independent of the live runtime. Its own renderer should own timing; its tests should observe output rather than restate timing constants.

verification.limits: No live browser or Aiur run; minimal DOM/API doubles and fake clock. No independent skeptic review yet.

findings.title: Capture readiness deadline does not bound an in-flight HTTP request
findings.description: The 30-second deadline is checked only before fetch. Neither fetch nor response.text receives a cancellation signal, so a stalled response prevents reaching the deadline check and the finally cleanup until that operation settles or its underlying transport fails. A successful response arriving after the deadline is accepted. The application-level deadline therefore does not enforce its advertised bound.
findings.evidence: An extracted, unmodified waitUntilReady with a fake clock remains pending at 31 seconds while fetch is unresolved; the fetch options contain no signal. Resolving the response with the fixture markers after that deadline returns success. This is a source-level controlled probe, not a measured production hang.
findings.recommendation: Apply an abort signal using the remaining deadline to the request and body read, and recheck the deadline before accepting readiness. Cover a connected response that never finishes, not only connection refusal.
findings.refactor_hint: Screenshot tooling owns fixture readiness and teardown. Keep those lifecycle obligations in its small harness instead of adding them to the production daemon.

verification.limits: No live browser or Aiur run; minimal DOM/API doubles and fake clock. No independent skeptic review yet.

findings.title: Copy control advances before confirming clipboard success
findings.description: The click handler discards copyText's promise, applies the copied class immediately, and expands shell next steps. When the modern clipboard rejects and execCommand returns false, copyText nevertheless resolves. The user can be directed to continue with an unchanged clipboard. The frozen CSS makes copied an accent state; this finding does not claim the button displays a literal success message.
findings.evidence: The extracted copyText function resolves with a rejected writeText and a false execCommand result; the fallback is called once. The actual click handler uses void copyText(command) before the copied class and show-next updates.
findings.recommendation: Return an explicit copy outcome, check execCommand's boolean, await completion in the click handler, and apply completion feedback only after success. Offer selectable command text on failure.
findings.refactor_hint: A local browser interaction fix; this does not justify a shared daemon clipboard service or a new package.

verification.limits: No live browser or Aiur run; minimal DOM/API doubles and fake clock. No independent skeptic review yet.

findings.title: A failed monitor spawn forks two recovery chains
findings.description: spawnLineSource forwards both error and close to onEnd. The runtime treats each as a separate terminal event, schedules a restart twice, and retains only the newest timer and child. When a monitor executable is absent, Node actually emits ENOENT followed by close(-2). The two timers create two replacements; stopping the runtime kills only the last replacement. If stopped before either timer runs, the overwritten timer remains and can spawn a child after stop. The normal main-process signal path calls process.exit after cleanup, so the post-stop survival claim applies to the exported runtime stop API; duplicate monitors while running do not depend on that API.
findings.evidence: streamdeck-lifecycle-probe.json: actual failed executable produces two onEnd calls; actual runtime schedules 500 and 1000 ms retries, creates two replacement sleep monitors, and leaves one replacement outside cleanup. The line-source test explicitly expects two notifications; the runtime harness registers only close, so its restart test misses the pair.
findings.recommendation: Make termination idempotent per monitor generation, retain one restart timer, and guard spawnOnce against stopped state. Test the error-then-close sequence through the composed source/runtime, including stopping before and after replacement.
findings.refactor_hint: Keep the pure device reducer. Strengthen the child-monitor adapter contract with exactly-once termination and generation-owned cleanup; splitting packages without that contract preserves the defect.

verification.limits: No physical USB or live daemon. Real Node missing-executable spawn confirms the monitor trigger; remaining collaborators are injected doubles. No independent skeptic review yet.

findings.title: Removing another Elgato product takes the active deck offline
findings.description: Device discovery/open selects VID and PID, but udev filtering accepts any usb_device with vendor 0fd9. A remove for another product therefore becomes device-removed for the connected Stream Deck +. The reducer closes the healthy handle and enters absent; there is no retry timer, so it waits for a later matching-vendor add event or restart despite the intended deck remaining plugged in. The trigger requires another same-vendor device; no prevalence is claimed.
findings.evidence: The composed runtime probe starts one healthy fake backend, ignores a different-vendor remove, then closes once on vendor 0fd9/product ffff and leaves zero poll/reopen timers. Product ffff is deliberately synthetic, not a claim about a shipped model. A proper 0084 removal is still recognized. Existing udev tests include different vendors and driver/interface churn, but no same-vendor different-product case.
findings.recommendation: Match the selected device identity across discovery and hotplug. At minimum check product as well as vendor; for multiple identical devices, correlate the owned physical device path or serial. Add composed add/remove tests for other products and other instances of the same model.
findings.refactor_hint: Device selection and hotplug normalization need one identity contract. Do not pass a cause-neutral vendor event to a lifecycle that assumes it refers to its owned device.

verification.limits: No physical USB or live daemon. Real Node missing-executable spawn confirms the monitor trigger; remaining collaborators are injected doubles. No independent skeptic review yet.

findings.title: Send discards spoken text before delivery is accepted
findings.description: sendTranscript optional-chains the channel call and then unconditionally clears the voice buffer. With channel=null during reconnect, no frame is sent and the only buffered text is discarded. With a connected channel, say refs are not tracked, so a server error or outcome_unknown reply has no callback and cannot preserve/recover the already-cleared message. main.ts retains the live grid on disconnect and voiceSession.dispose stops capture without clearing committed text, so the offline case is reachable with a retained Send affordance.
findings.evidence: streamdeck-channel-probe.json: encoded key input against the actual controller changes nonempty text to empty with a null channel. A say error frame against the actual channel generates zero callbacks, while an answer_command error invokes commandsError as a positive parsing control. Server reply_to_say explicitly returns errors and outcome_unknown.
findings.recommendation: Represent an outbound message as pending until a correlated server receipt, keep text and a stable message ID through disconnect/unknown outcomes, and expose failure without consuming the buffer. Reject offline sends visibly. Do not regenerate the message ID for a retry of the same intended message.
findings.refactor_hint: The channel API currently returns void for a durable delivery operation. Make submission, receipt and unknown outcome explicit in the device-control contract rather than relying on UI optimism.

verification.limits: Encoded HID input and synthetic socket replies against frozen source; injected voice/channel ports and extracted agentLess predicate. No renderer, hardware or live daemon. No independent skeptic review yet.

findings.title: Implement shows QUEUED when no request was sent or a request failed
findings.description: The Implement handler sets implementQueued after an optional channel call, even when the channel is null. The rendered key derives QUEUED from that flag. When connected, control replies are untracked and errors are ignored; the flag clears on any grid update rather than on an operation result. A physical press can therefore claim queued before any daemon acceptance, and during reconnect can claim it without a request at all.
findings.evidence: The controller probe presses Implement with channel=null and observes implementQueued=true. The channel probe sends implement then an error reply and observes no callback. The server explicitly returns queue success or failure, so a receipt exists but is not consumed.
findings.recommendation: Keep a sending state separate from accepted queue state, disable or visibly reject offline control attempts, and correlate the control reply to the ticket/action before rendering QUEUED. Cover daemon rejection and disconnect as well as successful method invocation.
findings.refactor_hint: Share an explicit command-result contract across physical and browser surfaces. Keep client intent separate from daemon state.

verification.limits: Encoded HID input and synthetic socket replies against frozen source; injected voice/channel ports and extracted agentLess predicate. No renderer, hardware or live daemon. No independent skeptic review yet.

findings.title: Command history cannot advance beyond the server first page
findings.description: The server defaults to eight history items and supplies has_next/next_cursor. The channel exposes commandsPage(cursor), but the controller never calls it: both knob turning and pressing only clamp or cycle within commandsPage.items.length. An eight-item first page has maximum local offset zero, so the control advertised as history paging cannot reach older Commands. Merely retaining the unused channel method does not provide paging.
findings.evidence: The probe gives the actual controller eight items, total 24 and a next cursor, then drives four cycles of dial turns and presses. It makes zero commandsPage requests and historyOffset stays zero. Repository search finds the controller method name only in its channel type, not an invocation.
findings.recommendation: Consume the opaque cursor when navigation reaches the loaded-page boundary, keep page/focus identity and a previous-page strategy, and distinguish loading/error from end-of-history. Test using the server default eight-item page plus a next cursor, not a single oversized in-memory page.
findings.refactor_hint: Document whether the client holds one server page or accumulated history. The present local-window and server-cursor contracts are both implemented but never connected.

verification.limits: Encoded HID input and synthetic socket replies against frozen source; injected voice/channel ports and extracted agentLess predicate. No renderer, hardware or live daemon. No independent skeptic review yet.

findings.title: Key release discards the final transcript it asks the server to commit
findings.description: Release flushes audio and calls relay close, which removes the transcript handler before port.stop. The host sends voice_stop then clears its session ID. The server commits asynchronously and forwards the settled final, but both client layers have already stopped accepting it. Text settled before release survives; the remaining partial is dropped even if its final arrives successfully. This concerns the tail not already settled by provider VAD, not every utterance.
findings.evidence: Composed source probe shows already settled last words before release and only already settled after a matching final. Direct relay delivery after release also fails, so retaining the host ID alone cannot repair the contract. Server realtime commit waits for settled text and notifies final before finishing. Relay tests explicitly require dropping every post-close final; session tests settle text before release.
findings.recommendation: Separate ending audio input from completing transcription. Retain generation-scoped handlers until final/closed or a bounded failure deadline; retain unsettled text with an explicit state. Test release followed by final through the composed host/relay/session.
findings.refactor_hint: Give the audio boundary a finishing state and a completion contract shared with the server; a synchronous close interface cannot represent asynchronous settlement.

verification.limits: Actual client link/relay/session, injected capture/channel and ordered synthetic replies. No provider, physical microphone or live daemon; no independent skeptic review.

findings.title: A delayed voice start reply consumes audio from the next hold
findings.description: If hold A is released before its start reply and hold B begins before that reply arrives, start resets the only queue and stop intent. The reply for A is accepted as the currently open hold, and queued B audio is labelled session A. The later B reply changes the ID again. Ordered replies are sufficient; no network reordering is required. The channel tracks refs but omits request identity from voiceStarted. The server replaces its active session on each start, so mislabelled frames may be discarded rather than transcribed.
findings.evidence: The probe drives hold A, buffered audio, release, hold B, buffered audio, then ordered A/B replies. A audio disappears, B audio is sent under A, and only B gets a stop. A synthetic A transcript is also accepted during this interval; that proves the client guard limitation, not that the server necessarily emits such a frame.
findings.recommendation: Carry a hold/request generation through voiceStart and its callback, and preserve or explicitly cancel each pending hold. Route audio, stop intent and completion to the matching generation; test overlapping holds with delayed ordered replies.
findings.refactor_hint: Session IDs minted by the server do not replace client request identity during the pre-reply interval.

verification.limits: Actual client link/relay/session, injected capture/channel and ordered synthetic replies. No provider, physical microphone or live daemon; no independent skeptic review.

findings.title: Capture discards recorder bytes flushed by its requested stop
findings.description: The Node adapter sends SIGINT specifically to flush buffered recorder audio, but capture sets stopped before signalling and drops every later stdout chunk. Session release immediately flushes only already-delivered bytes and closes transcription. Bytes buffered before key release are therefore discarded if they arrive during recorder shutdown. This is distinct from rejecting a final transcript after successful upload (finding 09).
findings.evidence: A bounded real Node child emits [1,0], then flushes [2,0] on SIGINT. The actual Node system adapter sees all four bytes, while the composed capture/session forwards only [1,0] without an error. Existing capture test requires discarding post-stop chunks; node-system test proves SIGINT but does not compose capture. This establishes the consumer defect conditional on a recorder tail, not the number of bytes parec buffers on real hardware.
findings.recommendation: Represent stop-requested and drained as separate capture states. Deliver buffered bytes through recorder exit, then flush the aggregator and commit transcription, with bounded forced cleanup and hold identity. Replace contradictory isolated expectations with a composed drain-before-commit test.
findings.refactor_hint: An audio lifecycle boundary must own both process termination and drain completion; changing only the signal or package name preserves loss.

verification.limits: Actual frozen source. Capture has a real bounded Node child, not microphone/parec; playback events and fetch response are injected. No hardware/provider/daemon, incident prevalence or independent skeptic review.

findings.title: Unused playback adapter can hang on sink failure and conceal exit errors
findings.description: A write that returns false waits only for drain. A subsequent stdin error or process exit marks the sink dead but never settles the pending write, so playEncodedAudio cannot reach its finally/close. Separately close resolves even for nonzero exit. No production caller was found for these helpers in the frozen repository, so this is a latent library defect rather than an observed device outage.
findings.evidence: Injected sink returns false, then emits error and exit(1). After the event loop drains, playback remains pending and close has not run; only a synthetic drain unblocks it. A separate exit(9) closes successfully. Tests cover drain, exit and stdin failure individually, but not failure during backpressure; the real-child test does not await its write.
findings.recommendation: Before wiring this code into a product, reject pending writes on terminal failure and report failed exits. Decide whether the unused playback/TTS code belongs in the package at all before investing in its API.
findings.refactor_hint: Do not infer adoption or extract a new package merely because unused adapters have tests.

verification.limits: Actual frozen source. Capture has a real bounded Node child, not microphone/parec; playback events and fetch response are injected. No hardware/provider/daemon, incident prevalence or independent skeptic review.

findings.title: Unused fetch adapter does not cancel a body when streaming stops
findings.description: Breaking the fetch adapter async iterator releases its reader lock without cancelling the body. The TTS contract promises cancellation when the iterator is abandoned, and playback documentation claims that ceasing to await its Promise guarantees release; neither is an implemented cancellation protocol. These helpers have no production callers in the frozen source, so no live provider or cost impact is claimed.
findings.evidence: Using an actual local ReadableStream and synthetic fetch, the probe breaks after one chunk: cancel is never called, the body is unlocked, and more bytes remain enqueueable/readable. It explicitly cancels the body during probe cleanup. This proves missing body cancellation, not whether a remote provider stops billing on HTTP cancellation.
findings.recommendation: Use explicit abort/cancel ownership, cancel the response body when iteration ends early, and document the difference between breaking iteration and abandoning an awaited Promise. Test cancellation while reading and while writing if these helpers are retained.
findings.refactor_hint: A stream return value is not by itself a resource ownership contract.

verification.limits: Actual frozen source. Capture has a real bounded Node child, not microphone/parec; playback events and fetch response are injected. No hardware/provider/daemon, incident prevalence or independent skeptic review.

findings.title: Microphone paging changes the displayed active device without changing capture
findings.description: The compositor finds selectedMic only among the visible six microphone slots. If the selected device is on another page, the settings strip falls back to microphones[0], even though capture resolves the selected ID against the full device list. Paging alone therefore makes the active microphone caption name the wrong device. Selecting a non-first device and paging away is sufficient.
findings.evidence: The actual compositor, with a recording rasterizer and no-op transport, receives eight microphones and selectedMicId mic-7. Page offsets 6,0,6 yield strip selectedLabel Mic 7,Mic 0,Mic 7. The selection never changes. main.ts constructs capture from micPreferences.resolve over all device IDs. This verifies the panel model, not rendered pixels or microphone hardware.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the selected microphone against the complete device list for the strip caption. Keep page slicing for key placement only. Test a selected device outside the visible page and a remembered device that is absent.
findings.refactor_hint: Separate active-device identity from the currently visible selection window; a shared page model is not the full device state.

verification.limits: Actual compositor/layout with recording encoder, no-op writes; no native rendering, USB, microphone or independent skeptic review.

unpromoted_observations.disposition: Not established as a privacy leak. Some ambient credential names are not stripped, but fixture initialization installs synthetic readers, avoids live provider-meter startup, and disables GitHub quota refresh. A retained environment name alone is insufficient evidence of real data reaching screenshots.
No demonstrated teardown failure. Need actual child/process behavior before promoting the unbounded exit wait to a finding.
Potential geometry mismatch: side-by-side uses aspect ratio and a minimum 44-column pane beside a 30-column dashboard. Needs browser reachability/layout evidence before claiming clipping.

stop calls cleanup without closing the backend or changing reducer state. Production main uses the registered signal handler instead. Review API consumers before separately promoting this beyond the monitor timer behavior demonstrated in finding 04.

main.ts and vitest.config.ts call the entry point branch-free wiring, but it now contains buffering, async device acquisition, voice rebuilds, channel retry state and rendering coordination. Coverage exclusion is real; absence of all integration protection is not established yet. Channel/controller/surface tests remain to read.
startInput runs outside the iface.claim try/catch. A synchronous startPoll exception may retain the opened handle. Need adapter-level reproduction and caller cleanup audit before promoting.

A synthetic join error causes neither closed notification nor socket close; subsequent controls remain pending. Source has no join/heartbeat acknowledgement deadline. Need deployment reachability and transport/server close behavior before asserting indefinite live failure.

approveCommand clears dictation and selection before answer receipt, including a null-channel case after async key derivation. Related to finding 06, but the answer flow and focus races need their own composed probe before broadening its scope.

setCommands accepts page identity without matching focusedIdentifier; setLogs stores previousStarts after replacing eventStarts. Trace actual push ordering and sliding-window tests before promoting either candidate.
Promoted to finding 11 after composed real-child drain reproduction; hardware prevalence remains unmeasured.
Promoted as latent P3 findings 12 and 13. Full tests read; no production caller or public-barrel export found, so no live device or quota impact claimed.

audio/index.ts describes the whole directory as provider-free and self-contained, but the unused elevenlabs-tts.ts accepts a credential and imports ../aiur-speech.js. The actual barrel omits TTS/playback. Carry this distinction into package planning: the active barrel is narrower than the directory. This is not evidence of a runtime credential leak.

decodePcm16 drops an odd trailing byte without carrying it to the next chunk; raw bytes still reach the transcriber through the aggregator, so potential misalignment affects meters/waveform, not necessarily transcription. Need split-stream composed evidence and production chunk census before broader impact claims.

KeyCache and KeyWriteQueue already distinguish pending/committed content, commit after full transfer, invalidate partial writes, halt after first-report failure, and require a fresh writer to reset. Full tests cover same-key reversal/cancellation. Preserve this contract when simplifying rendering; do not classify it as gratuitous layering.

unpromoted_observations.topic: Strip cache and repaint signature failures
unpromoted_observations.disposition: PanelCache records bytes before transport and surface records lastSignature before writes. main routes write failures to runtime recovery and surface invalidates on backend identity change, so the local eager-cache observation alone does not establish permanently stale production pixels. Need failure/recovery composition before promotion.

The typewriter uses row index/body, not role or stable event identity, and does not restrict message animation to assistant role despite a test comment. Inspect caller filtering and sliding transcript behavior before assigning user impact.
